key_idea: A dose d works iff d divides n, d <= k and n/d <= p, so enumerate divisors by trial division up to sqrt(n).
sketch: Loop d from 1 while d*d <= n (about 3.2e5 iterations for n = 1e11); for each divisor test both d and n/d against d <= k and n/d <= p, avoiding the double count when d*d == n. Sort and print the count then the values. O(sqrt n). Pitfalls: 64-bit integers everywhere, and the perfect-square duplicate.
